chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

We were in his presence, and in his presence was Humran, when a slave of his entered and said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is Ikrama in the throes of death' — and he used to hold the views of the Kharijites, but he was also devoted to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him). So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to us: 'Wait for me until I return to you.' And we said: 'Yes.' He was not long before he returned, and said: 'Know that had I reached Ikrama before the soul had settled at its place, I would have taught him certain words he would have benefitted by. But I found him and the soul had already settled at its place.'

I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! And what is that speech?' He said: 'It is, by God, what you all hold. Therefore, instruct your dying ones at the time of death with the testimony that there is no god except God, and the Wilayah.'

key_terms.الْخَوَارِج: The Kharijites — a sect that rebelled against Imam Ali and held takfiri views, here used to describe Ikrama's ideological position
key_terms.الْوَلَايَة: Wilayah — the authority, guardianship, and spiritual mandate of the Imams from the Ahl al-Bayt; here presented as essential for the dying testimony
key_terms.لَقِّنُوا مَوْتَاكُمْ: Instruct/prompt your dying ones — the obligation of talqeen (recitation of key beliefs at the moment of death)
key_terms.مَوْقِع النَّفْس: The settling place of the soul — an expression for the moment when the soul reaches the throat at the time of death, beyond which talqeen is no longer effective

ai.seo_question: What should be recited to a dying Muslim according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates how he rushed to the deathbed of Ikrama, a man who held Kharijite views yet was also devoted to the Imam. He arrived too late, finding the soul had already departed. This gave rise to an important ruling: believers must administer the talqeen (prompting) of the two testimonies — the declaration of tawhid and the Wilayah of the Imams — to the dying before the soul departs. The hadith reflects the Shia theological understanding that acknowledgment of the Wilayah is an integral part of the declaration of faith required at the moment of death.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘We were in his<sup>asws</sup> presence, and in his<sup>asws</sup> presence was Humran, when a slave of his<sup>asws</sup> came over, and he said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! This Ikrama is in (pangs of) death, and he views with the views of the Kharijites, and he was (also) devoted to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>’. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> said to us: ‘Wait for me<sup>asws</sup> until I<sup>asws</sup> return to you’. So we said, ‘Yes’. 
So it was not long before he<sup>asws</sup> returned, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, had I<sup>asws</sup> seen Ikrama before the soul had reached its place, I<sup>asws</sup> would have taught him ceratin words he would have benefitted by. But I<sup>asws</sup> saw him, and the soul had already reached its place’.

I said, ‘And what is that speech?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, what you all are upon, therefore indoctrinate your dying ones during the death, the testimony that there is no god except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and the Wilayah’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the above Hadith) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Qasim ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn abu ffamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “

Humran and we were present before abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a servant came in. He said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, ‘Ikrimah is in dying condition and he believes in the point of view of the al-Khawarij. However, he is (also) inclined to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam .’ The Imam then said to us, ’Wait until I return to you.’ We agreed and after a while the Imam returned and said, ’Had I met ‘Ikrimah before the soul reached where it was to reach, I could have taught him the words that would have benefitted him but I met him when the soul had already reached where it was to reach.’

I then asked, ’May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, what are those words?’ The Imam said, ’They, by Allah, are the (testimonies) of your belief. You must dictate to those in dying condition the testimony, “It is Allah alone who must be worshipped, and al-Walayah” (belief in the fact that ’A’immah possess Divine Authority).”’
